subject: Workplace Skills
title: The Cost of a Bad Meeting
description: A fast breakdown of The Cost of a Bad Meeting for builders.

hook.text: A Harvard study estimated that unnecessary meetings cost US companies $37 billion per year in lost productivity.

buildup.text: Most people attend 62 meetings per month. Half are considered a waste of time by participants.

discovery.text: The real cost is not just the hour. It is the interrupted focus, the context-switching, and the delayed deep work.

twist.text: Nobody wants bad meetings, yet they persist. The problem is rarely intent. It is design.

climax.text: Calculate meeting cost: multiply attendees by their hourly rate by duration. Share it once. Watch behavior shift.

punchline.text: Bad meetings are a design failure, not a people failure.

quiz.question: What is the hidden cost of unnecessary meetings beyond the time spent?
options: Higher electricity bills from conference rooms
Interrupted focus, context-switching, and delayed deep work
Increased commuting time for in-office workers
